title: WO INT8 compatibility: kernel-swap simulations and shadow evaluators
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: Validate end-to-end compatibility of INT8 weight-only profiles (GPTQ/AWQ) across kernel permutations and runtime kernel swaps, and provide a shadow-eval regression harness that runs in parallel with production traffic. This ticket focuses on (1) simulating kernel-swaps (e.g., switching matmul/convolution kernels and quantized microkernels) to detect numerical stability regressions, (2) exercising calibration variance (scale/zero-point perturbations) across a representative prompt set, and (3) building a shadow evaluation pipeline that computes semantic and token-level deltas without impacting serving latency. Deliverables include a reproducible test harness, automated nightly drift reports, and a canary playbook with rollback criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Shadow-eval harness runs on a mirrored sample of 5% production requests with <2% cost overhead
Per-model tolerance matrices defined (semantic-similarity threshold, token-level delta threshold) and stored in the quant-profile registry
Kernel-swap simulation exercise produces deterministic failure flags for out-of-tolerance models and writes a prioritized remediation list
Calibration perturbation sweep shows stability bounds (max allowed scale drift) and updates calibration pipeline defaults if needed
End-to-end integration tests (CI) that assert no regressions on golden-seed prompts for 20 curated models
Rollback playbook validated in staging with automated fallback to FP16 or a listed compatible INT8 variant
test_plan: 1) Unit: add kernel-swap unit tests to the runtime test-suite that instantiate model with KernelA then dynamically swap to KernelB and assert outputs within numeric tolerance

2) Integration: run GPTQ and AWQ quantized artifacts through the calibration perturbation harness (±10% scale, random bias offsets) and measure token-logprob drift and semantic similarity (embedding cosine)
3) Shadow-eval: wire a traffic mirror for a 24-hour window to run requests against INT8 variants; collect answer hashes, embeddings, token-stream diffs, and latency percentiles
4) Regression: add nightly job to run the curated golden-seed set across the quant-profile registry; fail CI on >3 models exceeding thresholds
5) Chaos: inject a kernel mismatch (simulate old kernel + new runtime flags) in staging and verify canary rollback triggers
6) Observability: add dedicated dashboards for per-model drift, percent out-of-tolerance, and total compute cost of shadow evaluations
telemetry_and_alerts: Emit 'quant_profile.drift' metric with tags {model, variant, kernel} recording semantic-similarity and token-delta
Alert (SEV2) if >5% requests in shadow-eval exceed model-specific tolerance within a 15m window
Create a PagerDuty policy for canary-fallback failures with a runbook link
Daily summary email with top 10 drifting models and recommended remediations
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Unit + integration tests in CI; gate: green CI for the test matrix
Stage 2: Staging shadow-eval at 100% of staging traffic for 48 hours; run kernel-swap stress tests
Stage 3: Gradual production mirror (1% -> 5% -> 5% rolling) for 7 days; evaluate drift metrics
Stage 4: Soft canary: route 0.5% live production traffic for latency and correctness checks with automated rollback if latency > SLO or drift > threshold
Stage 5: Full production enablement for supported models and update quant-profile registry
implementation_notes: Build a lightweight edge-side hook to mirror requests to the shadow-eval cluster to avoid influencing production latency
Shadow-eval must sample deterministic seeds for generation to make diffs comparable across runs
Use semantic similarity (embedding cosine) + normalized token-level Levenshtein to detect meaningful regressions; avoid raw token-only heuristics
Calibration sweeps should be parametrized so QA can reproduce failing buckets and replay with different seeds/temperatures
Ensure kernel-swap tests exercise both fused and unfused attention kernels and fallback math paths for int8 ops
